## Goal

Make the proxy respect MunitoAI's `x-ratelimit-*` response headers so it
stops probing the endpoint with requests that are guaranteed to be rejected
during a rate-limit exhaustion window, computing a proper cooldown from the
upstream's own reset timing instead of blind exponential backoff.

## Context / evidence (discovered 2026-10-16, from analysis of
`/var/log/llama-proxy` over the preceding 48h)

- MunitoAI 429 responses carry `{"error":{"message":"Too Many Requests","type":"rate_limit_error","param":null,"code":"rate_limit_exceeded"}}`
  and **no standard `Retry-After` header**, only custom headers, e.g.:
  `x-ratelimit-limit-requests: 10`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests: 0`,
  `x-ratelimit-reset-requests: 52s`, `x-ratelimit-over-limit: yes`
  (plus input/output/token variants).
- The proxy does not read any `x-ratelimit-*` header (verified: no code
  paths parse them). `_parse_retry_after` only handles `Retry-After`, which
  Munito never sends.
- Result: during the 48h window the endpoint returned 532 distinct failures
  (480 HTTP errors: 450×429, 15×400, 12×503, 3×502; 52 connect/read/empty).
  Because each 429 lands in the generic `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown`
  path (exponential backoff 1s→45s, capped at config
  `provider_cooldown_seconds: 60`), the proxy re-tries munitoai roughly every
  ≤45s during exhaustion — ~21,600 `Skipping provider=munitoai ... in
  cooldown` lines and repeated 429 bursts across the window, with traffic
  piling onto opencode-go-2 (388 falloffs). Munito's own reset header said
  52s on the live test request — far longer than the base 1s backoff.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: When a provider entry declares `respect_ratelimit_headers: true` (or
  the behaviour is enabled globally via `server.*` config), the proxy parses
  `x-ratelimit-reset-requests` / `x-ratelimit-reset-tokens` /
  `x-ratelimit-reset-input-tokens` / `x-ratelimit-reset-output-tokens` (and
  `x-ratelimit-over-limit`, if present) from an upstream HTTP 429 response.
- AC2: On a 429 with a parseable reset duration, the provider's cooldown is
  set to at least the reset duration (plus a small safety margin), replacing
  the pure exponential-backoff guess; per-provider failure counters are still
  respected so repeated failures extend the cooldown sensibly.
- AC3: On a 429 with `x-ratelimit-over-limit: yes` but no parseable reset,
  the behaviour falls back to the current exponential backoff unchanged (no
  regression for providers that only send `Retry-After` or nothing).
- AC4: The resolved cooldown is surfaced in the attempt record
  (`cooldown_seconds`) and the `Skipping provider=... in cooldown (Ns
  remaining)` log line reflects the header-derived duration.
- AC5: Unit tests cover: header parsing (seconds + optional unit suffixes
  like `52s`, `1m`, `1h30m`), the `x-ratelimit-over-limit` flag, precedence
  over backoff, fallback when headers are absent, and persistence of the
  header-derived cooldown in provider-state.json.
- AC6: Backward compatible: munitoai and all existing providers behave
  identically when the new config/flag is not enabled (default off).

## Out of scope

- Changing MunitoAI's quota/plan or renegotiating limits upstream.
- Surfacing `x-ratelimit-*` headers to proxy clients (though doing so is
  a cheap follow-up that could be noted).

## Related

- discovered-from: LP-0MV5UPXKL002MSKB (Add MunitoAI to fallback chains),
  LP-0MV6ENYYH006XX0Z (promote munitoai tier after local Qwen)
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MQ5NIBER002FJJY** – Cooldown/circuit breaker (completed)
- **LP-0MUIGX4HF003NWS5** – Persist provider state on mutation (completed)
- **LP-0MRCJD1WW0023AKX** – Exponential backoff for remote provider fallback cooldowns (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+164 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+164 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+164 more)
data.title: Proxy: honour MunitoAI x-ratelimit-* headers when queuing 429 cooldowns

# Evaluate whether `rate_limit_rpm` for `munitoai-free` should be increased

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want a measured answer to *"should `rate_limit_rpm` for
`munitoai-free` be raised above 10?"* — traded against upstream `429`s, the share
of traffic spilling to the paid `opencode` tiers, and latency — so the free tier
is used to the edge of its real allowance instead of spilling to paid capacity
for no reason (or being pushed past a limit that starts returning 429s).

## Context (current state, 2026-10-18)

- `rate_limit_rpm: 10` is declared on the three `munitoai-free` chain entries
  (`plan` / `author` / `code`) in `config.yaml` and the fast overlay — one shared
  bucket, because the limiter keys on the provider entry name (one account quota).
- `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3` → new sessions may use 7 of the 10
  slots; sessions already on the tier may use all 10 (`LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`).
- Waits are capped at 15 s, so over-budget requests now **spill** rather than
  queue. First ~4 min after that change at high demand (~19 remote dispatches/min):
  **20** free-tier vs **55** opencode dispatches (**73 % paid**), 35 new-session
  skips, 20 capped waits, 5 satisfied waits, **0** waits over 15 s.
- Upstream 429s: **0** since the 10/min gate went live. In the 12 h before the
  gate (bursts up to 72 dispatch/rolling-min) there were **19** MunitoAI
  429s (`rate_limit_exceeded`).
- Demand regularly exceeds 10/min, so some spill is arithmetically unavoidable
  at 10; the question is where the free tier's real knee sits.

## Evaluation method

1. **Establish demand** — the free-tier request rate per minute (p50/p95/max) and
   the share of minutes where demand exceeds the current budget.
2. **Find the knee** — measure upstream `429`/`rate_limit_exceeded` onset as a
   function of dispatch rate. Prefer evidence already in the logs (pre-gate
   bursts vs 429s); if a deliberate probe is needed, raise the budget
   incrementally (e.g. 10 → 12 → 15 → 20), one step per observation window
   (≥ 30 min at stable demand), and **stop at the first 429** — do not hammer a
   third-party free tier.
3. **Cost the spill** — count dispatches to `opencode`/`deepseek` attributable to
   `reason=rate_limited` / `rate_limited_after_wait` fallbacks per setting,
   expressed as a share of total remote dispatches.
4. **Latency** — confirms no regression: wait distribution stays ≤ 15 s, and
   p90/p95/p99 first-token latency for gated dispatches does not rise.
5. **Recommend** a value (keep 10 / 12 / 15 / 20 / header-derived) with the
   evidence table above; if it changes, implement it in this item with a
   documented observation window, or hand the decision to `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L`
   (derive the budget from `x-ratelimit-*` headers) if a static value cannot
   track the allowance.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A measurement table of demand, upstream 429s, spill share and wait/latency per
   candidate budget (at least the current 10 plus the knee value) is attached to
   this work item as a comment.
2. The free tier's approximate 429 onset (dispatches/rolling-60 s) is established
   from log evidence, or an explicit note says why it could not be established.
3. The share of remote dispatches going to each paid tier at each candidate is
   quantified (this is the cost of a too-conservative budget).
4. A single recommendation is recorded (keep / raise to N / lower / header-derived)
   with its expected effect on 429s, paid spill and latency.
5. If a new value is adopted: it is applied to `proxy/config.yaml` **and** the fast
   overlay for all three chains, the observation window is documented, a follow-up
   check-in item is created for 24 h later, and the full project test suite passes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect any change (config comments,
   `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`).

## Constraints

- Do not remove or weaken the gate or the reserve — this item tunes one number.
- Never drive a third-party free tier into sustained 429s to "measure the limit";
  incremental, bounded steps only, one step per window.
- Any config change goes through a worktree + test/build gate; a proxy restart is
  required for it to take effect and must be noted in the measurement timeline.
- Test runs go through the test skill.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — reserve + 15 s cap (the change that made spilling the
  default over-budget behaviour).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` — the original budget gate.
- `LP-0MVDU4FDE003RQHS` — scheduled full-window effectiveness evaluation (its
  3-sub-window analysis feeds this item).
- `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` — header-derived (`x-ratelimit-*`) budgeting, the
  alternative to a static number.


## Key Files

- proxy/config.yaml — rate_limit_rpm: 10 on the three munitoai-free chain entries (plan / author / code).
- proxy/config-fast.yaml — the fast overlay, same three entries.
- proxy/README.md, proxy/docs/routing.md — config/routing docs to update if the value changes.
- Proxy logs (rolling 24-48 h) — demand, 429 and fallback evidence used for the measurements.
data.title: Evaluate whether munitoai-free rate_limit_rpm should be increased

# Chain-hold on budget-window exhaustion: hold ~60s for the free-tier window to roll over (not hold 0s)

discovered-from: herdr-1792387482-2237208-25455 (audit of SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81, 2026-10-19)

## Problem (measured)

When a fallback chain exhausts because the `munitoai-free` sliding-window
request budget is momentarily full, the chain-hold wrapper holds **0s** and
fails all 3 cycles instantly, even though recovery is only the 60s window rollover
away. Audit Phase-2 (`audit-SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81-phase2_deep-ede9d520`) hit
`Pi provider error: "All providers exhausted"` twice + a failed verdict re-ask;
the verdict re-ask only succeeded minutes later once the window freed.

Proxy log (2026-10-19 ~07:23 local):

```
Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: 13/11 requests in 60s window
Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=munitoai-free limit=11 reserve=4 remaining=2 reason=rate_limited
All providers exhausted for model=v1/chat/completions; unavailable={}; usage_limit_reset=None
Chain exhausted for model=v1/chat/completions; holding 0s before restarting cycle ...
```

Root cause chain:

1. Local Qwen3 saturated (0/2 slots held by other sessions) → queue 120s → fallback.
2. `plan.priority_routes.low = [local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` only; budget skip is a
   **pre-check** that never adds a cooldown entry → exhaustion response has
   `unavailable={}` (no cooldown, no usage_limit_reset).
3. `_bounded_hold_seconds` (LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08) sees `retry_after <= 0` → returns
   **0.0** → `_run_chain_cycles` replays all `chain_hold_max_cycles` (3) cycles
   inside the same exhausted window → instant failure.

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, when a chain exhausts solely because a free-tier rolling
budget window is full (cooldown-free, `unavailable={}`), I want the chain-hold
wrapper to hold ~the window rollover (bounded by existing budgets) so the next
cycle can succeed once the window frees — instead of failing all cycles
instantly and surfacing a spurious "All providers exhausted" to clients.

## Desired change

- When a budget-skip exhaustion carries no cooldown/`usage_limit_reset` but the
  entry has a `rate_limit_rpm` window, derive a `retry_after` from the window
  rollover (≤ the configured wait bounds, e.g. `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds`)
  so `_bounded_hold_seconds` returns a positive hold instead of 0.0.
- Keep the "truly-retryable-now" case (real 0 cooldown) at 0s — no added latency.
- Respect `chain_hold_total_seconds` / client 900s ceiling.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — A chain whose only blockers are rate-limit budget skips yields a positive
  hold (~window rollover, subject to configured caps) rather than 0s, and the next
  cycle succeeds once the window frees (regression test modelled on the 13/11 scenario).
- **AC2** — Genuine instant-recovery exclusions (`retry_after == 0` from a real
  cooldown) still retry with no added latency (LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08 behaviour preserved).
- **AC3** — Cumulative hold stays within `chain_hold_total_seconds` and strictly
  below the client's 900s deadline (LP-0MV6BR3HI00957PF contract).
- **AC4** — The 503 exhaustion body carries an accurate `Retry-After`/`retry_after`
  derived from the window rollover so clients can back off correctly.

## References

- Code: `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_run_chain_cycles` (~5809), `_bounded_hold_seconds`
  (~5686), `_log_chain_hold_start` (~5600); budget skip in `provider_budget.py`.
- Related items: LP-0MSH94Z7K007VKC9 (chain-hold origin), LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08
  (hold bounded by retry_after — the 0.0 branch this item fixes), LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20
  (free-tier reserve + 15s wait for in-progress sessions; new sessions pass through),
  LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL (do not over-use munitoai-free), LP-0MVDNP36J006430L (upstream
  x-ratelimit reset headers — complementary, cooldown based).
data.title: Chain-hold on budget-window exhaustion: hold for the free-tier 60s window rollover, not 0s

data.description:
## Problem statement

The proxy's `low` priority route (used by the priority-window cheap slot, 01:00–10:00 local, plus any explicit `X-Priority: low`) currently chains as `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` for the plan/author/code models. When the 2 local slots are saturated (a common overnight condition — see the 2026-10-19 proxy-usage-analysis report: `fallback_after_queue` 1657, `large_context_bypass` 1530, `context_too_large` 3393), low-priority traffic falls straight through to `munitoai-free`, which is capped at **`rate_limit_rpm: 2`** and is the last entry in the chain — so once its tiny budget is spent the request has nowhere else to go but an upstream 429 (16 upstream 429 events in the last window, all from `api.munito.ai`).

Meanwhile the three `opencode-go` entries (`opencode-go-3`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go`) sit idle despite being available during their off-peak UTC windows (`["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`, added by LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P) — which are precisely the hours when the cheap priority window is active and local is most contended.

Goal: allow low-priority work to fall back to **all** opencode models while they are inside their permissible (`available_times`) windows, so local-slot overflow during cheap hours is absorbed by idle paid capacity instead of being rate-limited on the free tier.

## Operator decisions (recorded)

- **Do NOT widen `available_times`.** The existing off-peak windows stay exactly as they are; paid spend remains confined to them.
- **Allow all opencode models on the low chain**, gated by those windows — not just one entry.

## Context / constraints

- `priority_routes.low` for plan/author/code is `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` (`proxy/config.yaml`); `munitoai-free` carries `rate_limit_rpm: 2`.
- Each of plan/author/code defines three equivalent opencode entries: `opencode-go-3` (OPENCODE_3_API_KEY), `opencode-go-2` (OPENCODE_2_API_KEY), `opencode-go` (OPENCODE_API_KEY) — same gateway, same model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, same windows.
- **Why all three is meaningful (not cosmetic):** per LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW / LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N, rate-limit quarantine is keyed on the **API-key account** (`_usage_limit_account_key` = `api_key_env@endpoint`), *not* the shared gateway domain. A 429 on one entry therefore poisons only that account, so its sibling keys are still tried with their own independent quota — i.e. 3× rate-limit capacity.
- **Counter-caveat to document:** for *non-rate-limit* failures (5xx, stalls) same-gateway siblings ARE skipped as one failure domain (`_failure_domain_key` / `attempted_domains`), so the three entries do **not** multiply capacity during an opencode outage. That is correct behaviour and must be stated in the config comments so nobody expects 3× resilience.
- **UTC-vs-local alignment (measured):** `available_times` are **UTC**; the cheap window (01:00–10:00) is **local `Europe/Dublin` = UTC 00:00–09:00**. opencode-go is unavailable UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00, so the new tiers add capacity in **~3 of the 9 cheap hours** (UTC 00:00–01:00 and 04:00–06:00). Accepted — the gaps are deliberate paid-spend avoidance, and the operator chose not to widen them.
- The `compact` model's low chain (`opencode-go-compact → deepseek-flash-compact`) is out of scope.
- The fully-paid `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` entries must NOT join the low chain — they have no window discipline enforcing off-peak-only spend (`munitoai` has no `available_times` at all).

## Scope

Config + routing documentation + tests only. No llama-server changes, no `available_times` changes. Evidence via the proxy-usage-analysis skill (`python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24`).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `priority_routes.low` for plan, author and code chains **all three** opencode entries, ordered after `munitoai-free`: `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free, opencode-go-3, opencode-go-2, opencode-go]`.
2. Every `available_times` value in `proxy/config.yaml` is **unchanged** by this work (no widening) — verifiable by diffing the config for `available_times` lines.
3. Unit tests prove window gating: inside a window the opencode entries are eligible; outside, they are skipped and the chain falls through exactly as today.
4. Unit tests prove per-key 429 failover: a 429 on `opencode-go-3` does not exclude `opencode-go-2`/`opencode-go` from the same request (independent account quota), while a 5xx on `opencode-go-3` DOES exclude them as one failure domain.
5. Chain order preserved: `local-qwen3` first when local has capacity; `munitoai-free` before any paid entry; `medium`/`high` chains byte-identical to before.
6. `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` never appear in a `low` chain.
7. Config comments (and `priority.py::priority_routing_profile` docstring if it states the paid-tier invariant) document: the off-peak exception, the 3-of-9-hour UTC/local overlap, the per-key-429 capacity rationale, and the same-domain 5xx caveat.
8. Full suite passes via `/skill:test`; a post-change proxy-usage-analysis report is recorded on this item showing whether `rate_limited`/HTTP 429 from `api.munito.ai` fell during the overlap hours, with an honest "too small a sample" statement if not.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I** – Add opencode-go to low-priority routes (off-peak) (blocked)
- **LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1** – Test: off-peak low-priority fallback gating (open)
- **LP-0MVBJXZY5002UW10** – start-proxy.sh auth.json key lookup does not match the documented munitoai-free name (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0msmbwb23009xypw, 0mvcx0e2v001vb5n, 5xx, acceptance, accepted (+187 more)
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 5xx, accepted, account, active, add (+181 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: acceptance, accepted, account, active, add (+175 more)

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/config.yaml` — set `priority_routes.low` for `plan` (line 410), `author` (line 528) and `code` (line 653) to `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free, opencode-go-3, opencode-go-2, opencode-go]`; add the off-peak-window exception, per-key-429 capacity and same-domain-5xx caveat comments. Every `available_times` line must stay byte-identical.
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — `priority_routing_profile` (line 270) docstring: record the off-peak paid-tier exception where the paid-tier invariant is stated.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — reused read-only: `_is_within_allowed_window` (line 2376, UTC window gate), `_usage_limit_account_key` (line 4358, per-account 429 quarantine), `_failure_domain_key` (line 4245, same-gateway 5xx skip).
- `proxy/tests/` — new window-gating, chain-order, per-key-429 and same-domain-5xx tests (owned by LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1).

## Effort and risk

- **Effort: S** — config edit + doc comments + tests; no new routing mechanism (`_is_within_allowed_window` already gates the chain).
- **Risk: Low** — window gate makes the change behaviour-neutral outside the off-peak windows; append-only chain change, fully reversible by removing three list entries.
- Recorded at the plan stage; the intake review changed no scope, so the estimate stands.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded from the `plan` session (comment `LP-C0MVF1G18A000NAJ0`), re-confirmed during this intake review.

### Q1. Which opencode-go entry joins the low chain?
`proxy/config.yaml` defines three equivalent entries: `opencode-go-3` (`OPENCODE_3_API_KEY`), `opencode-go-2` (`OPENCODE_2_API_KEY`), `opencode-go` (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`) — same gateway, same model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, identical `available_times`.
**Answer (operator):** all three, ordered `opencode-go-3 → opencode-go-2 → opencode-go`, after `munitoai-free`. Rationale: rate-limit quarantine is per API-key account (`_usage_limit_account_key`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py:4075`), so sibling keys carry independent quota → 3× rate-limit capacity. Evidence: comment `LP-C0MVF1O13P001N6RO`.

### Q2. UTC vs local window alignment — widen `available_times`?
`available_times` are **UTC**; the priority cheap window (01:00–10:00) is local `Europe/Dublin` = UTC 00:00–09:00. opencode-go is unavailable UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 → the new tiers add capacity in ~3 of 9 cheap hours (UTC 00:00–01:00, 04:00–06:00).
**Answer (operator):** do **not** widen the windows; paid spend stays confined to the existing off-peak windows and the 3-of-9 overlap is the accepted benefit. Evidence: `proxy/config.yaml` `available_times` (added by LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P); comment `LP-C0MVF1O13P001N6RO`.

### Q3. Should the `compact` model's low chain change?
`compact` already chains `low: [opencode-go-compact, deepseek-flash-compact]` (`proxy/config.yaml` ~line 658) — no local tier, opencode already leads.
**Answer (eng):** no — out of scope, leave untouched.

### Q4. Do the fully paid `munitoai` / `deepseek-flash` entries join the low chain?
**Answer (operator/eng):** no. They carry no window discipline enforcing off-peak-only spend (`munitoai` has no `available_times` at all). Pinned as AC6.

### Duplicate-work check (this intake run)
`wl search` on `opencode-go`, `off-peak`, `low priority`, `priority_routes`, `munitoai` reviewed. Nearest neighbours: LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P (added the off-peak windows — prerequisite, completed), LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA (introduced priority routing with `low = local + free`, completed), LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW / LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N (per-account quarantine — basis for AC4, completed). **No duplicate:** no existing item adds opencode-go entries to a `low` chain.

Two neighbours worth cross-referencing (neither duplicates this scope):

- **LP-0MVF0N9SA0071LWM** (in progress) — chain-hold on `munitoai-free` 60s budget-window exhaustion holds 0s and fails the chain instantly. Adding windowed opencode entries after `munitoai-free` gives the chain somewhere else to go, but does not replace the hold fix; sequence independently, no shared file beyond `provider.py` chain iteration (read-only here).
- **LP-0MVELM2NN006I0AU** (completed, `test-failure`) — legacy fast/cheap-mode assertions in `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` / `test_provider_fallback.py` were rewritten for priority routing. The new gating tests (LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1) should extend those post-rewrite tests, not the removed fast-mode expectations.

### AC coverage review (this intake run)
`run_coverage_review(LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX)` → `recommendation: proceed` — all 8 acceptance criteria are covered by the three children (test LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1, config LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I, live verification LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO); no gaps, no conflicts.

# Reduce `munitoai-free` request budget to 2/minute

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want the `munitoai-free` provider entry to dispatch at
most **2** requests per rolling 60-second window (down from 15), so the free tier
is used sparingly and traffic spills to the paid tiers rather than burning the
quiet free allowance on bursts.

## Scope

- `proxy/config.yaml`: `rate_limit_rpm: 15` → `rate_limit_rpm: 2` on all three
  `munitoai-free` entries (plan / author / code).
- Docs that quote the shipped value: `proxy/docs/routing.md` (ships-with value +
  value history), `proxy/README.md` (reserve arithmetic `11 of 15`).
- No change to the gate, reserve, wait caps or any other provider.

## Notes

- With `rate_limit_rpm: 2` and `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3`,
  `floor(2 × 0.3) = 0` reserve slots, so new and in-progress sessions both see a
  cap of 2 per window (the reserve clamps to `rpm - 1`).
- Takes effect on the next proxy restart.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All three `munitoai-free` entries in `proxy/config.yaml` declare
   `rate_limit_rpm: 2`.
2. `proxy/docs/routing.md` and `proxy/README.md` state the shipped value of 2 and
   describe the resulting reserve/cap arithmetic correctly.
3. The changed-scope test gate passes (config-loading / fallback-chain tests).
4. Commit recorded on this work item and pushed to `dev`.
data.title: Reduce munitoai-free rate_limit_rpm to 2

# Quota poller and derived state (tracer bullet)

## Goal

Give the proxy a proactive, authoritative per-account view of each
`opencode-*` account's remaining allowance, instead of learning about
exhaustion reactively from a `GoUsageLimitError`.

This is the tracer bullet for LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P: it lands the module, the
injectable test transport (the shared harness every later feature is tested
through), the derivation model, the poll-interval config key and the
background poll task — end to end, with tests, in one slice.

## Scope

- New module `proxy/quota_state.py`:
  - `QuotaWindow` / `QuotaSnapshot` dataclasses holding
    `rolling`/`weekly`/`monthly` `percent` + `resetsAt`, plus derived
    `*_headroom`, `seconds_to_reset`, `effective_headroom`, `exhausted`,
    `last_success_at`, `last_status`.
  - Async poller for `GET {endpoint}/v1/usage` with `Authorization: Bearer
    $api_key_env`, `cache-control: no-store` honoured, per-account cache keyed
    on the API-key account (reuse `provider._usage_limit_account_key`
    semantics, not the endpoint).
  - Single-flight coalescing per account (one in-flight task per account) and
    interval gating on `server.quota_poll_interval_seconds` (default 900).
  - Injectable module-level transport hook (mirroring
    `provider._usage_limit_probe_transport`) so tests never touch the network.
  - Fail-open on poll error: keep the last known snapshot, log at WARN, never
    raise and never delay a client request.
- Derivation rules: headroom is `100 - percent` per window;
  `effective_headroom` is the **minimum** of the three; a window whose
  `status` is anything other than `"ok"` is treated conservatively as
  exhausted/blocking; a missing or unparseable `resetsAt` yields
  `seconds_to_reset <= 0` (never a guessed value).
- Config: `server.quota_poll_interval_seconds` [900] and
  `server.quota_surge_accounts` (optional filter; default = all `opencode-*`
  entries).
- Startup: register the refresh task in `proxy/lifecycle.py` and cancel it on
  shutdown; a failed poll must never break startup.
- Logging: one INFO line per successful poll per account (percent per window +
  seconds to reset); WARN on failure (rate-limited so a dead endpoint does not
  flood the log).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — With a stubbed `/v1/usage` transport, the poller issues at most one
  request per account per `server.quota_poll_interval_seconds` (default 900 s)
  no matter how many client requests arrive, and concurrent pollers coalesce
  into a single in-flight request per account.
- AC1b — A poll failure (500, timeout, malformed body) leaves the previous
  values intact, logs at WARN, and never fails or delays a client request.
- AC2a — From a known `/v1/usage` payload the derived state reports, per
  account, `rolling`/`weekly`/`monthly` percent, `resetsAt`,
  `seconds_to_reset` and `effective_headroom`, where `effective_headroom` is
  the **minimum** of the three windows (feed `rolling=95, weekly=10,
  monthly=40` and assert effective headroom is 5).
- AC2b — A window whose `status` is not `"ok"` is treated conservatively as
  blocking (`exhausted`), and a missing/invalid `resetsAt` yields
  `seconds_to_reset <= 0` rather than a guessed value.
- AC1c — Two provider entries sharing one `api_key_env` share one account
  snapshot and one poll (no duplicate upstream `/v1/usage` calls).

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `proxy/quota_state.py` with dataclasses, derivation helpers and the
   poller; keep all clocks injectable (`now: Callable[[], datetime]`) so tests
   are deterministic.
2. Expose `get_quota_snapshot(provider_cfg, config)` (cache read, never
   blocking) and `refresh_quota_accounts(model_config, config)` (background
   refresh).
3. Wire the refresh task into `proxy/lifecycle.py` startup/shutdown.
4. Tests in `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py` using the injected transport and
   a frozen clock: interval gating, single-flight, fail-open, derivation
   (including the minimum-of-three case), shared-account de-duplication.

## Key Files

- `proxy/quota_state.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py`
- `proxy/lifecycle.py`
- `proxy/provider.py`

## Dependencies

None — this is the tracer bullet for the epic.

## Deliverables

- `proxy/quota_state.py` (poller + derivation + injectable transport harness)
- `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py` (unit + harness fixtures reused by later
  features)
- `server.quota_poll_interval_seconds` and `server.quota_surge_accounts`
  config keys (documented later in the docs feature)
- Poll logging (INFO success / WARN failure)

## Test plan

- Fake `/v1/usage` transport returning a fixed payload; frozen clock.
- Interval gating: 10 client calls inside one interval → 1 upstream poll.
- Single-flight: 5 concurrent refreshes → 1 in-flight request.
- Failure paths: 500, timeout, malformed JSON → previous snapshot retained,
  WARN logged, no exception escapes.
- Derivation table including `rolling=95, weekly=10, monthly=40 → 5`, a
  non-`ok` status, and a missing `resetsAt`.

# Intake Brief: F1 — Per-entry context-limit tests (test-first)

**Headline:** Write the failing test coverage for the per-entry
`max_context_tokens` gate **before** any implementation lands, plus config
parsing pinning, so F2 has a red-to-green target and the shipped semantics
are locked by tests.

## Goal

Prove, with meaningful assertions, that an entry whose configured
`max_context_tokens` is exceeded is skipped without failure side effects,
that at-or-below-limit entries are dispatched, and that ungated entries and
local chains behave byte-for-byte as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests (new `proxy/tests/test_provider_context_limit.py`, plus extensions to `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py` and `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`) cover, with meaningful assertions: (a) an entry above its limit is skipped with the correct reason; (b) an entry at or below its limit is dispatched; (c) absent/`0` limit is ungated; (d) a skip falls through to the next provider; (e) no cooldown/affinity/usage-limit state is applied after a skip; (f) local chains are unaffected; (g) config-parsing of the new field.
- Tests reference the agreed vocabulary: field `max_context_tokens`, skip status `provider_context_exceeded` (as recorded in the parent plan Appendix).
- The new tests are red against current behaviour (they describe the upcoming gate) and are wired into the suite so they run in the changed-scope gate.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_provider_context_limit.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`

## Dependencies

None (first item; prerequisite for F2).

# Intake Brief: F2 — Implement the `max_context_tokens` gate

**Headline:** Add the optional per-entry `max_context_tokens` provider field,
a reader + gate helper in `proxy/provider.py`, and enforce the skip in both
fallback dispatch loops **before** `acquire_provider_budget`/dispatch.

## Goal

Requests whose estimated prompt context exceeds an entry's configured limit
fall through to the next eligible provider, with no cooldown/affinity/
usage-limit/queue side effects and no duplicate tokenizer pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Provider entries accept an optional integer `max_context_tokens` defining the maximum estimated prompt context the entry may serve; absent, `0`, or non-positive disables the gate (behaviour byte-for-byte as today).
- In both fallback dispatch loops (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`), an entry whose `max_context_tokens` is exceeded by the request's estimated prompt tokens is skipped **before** `acquire_provider_budget`/dispatch, and the chain proceeds to the next eligible provider.
- The skip is recorded as a request attempt (status `provider_context_exceeded`) carrying the estimated tokens and the entry limit, and logged with the provider name, estimate, limit and reason.
- The estimate reuses the existing authoritative routing pipeline (`_get_tokenizer_for_model` + `_estimate_effective_prompt_tokens_for_routing` + `token_estimate_multiplier`) so the per-entry gate is consistent with the local gates and the hard routing cap; the estimate is computed once per request (per cycle) without a duplicate tokenizer pass per provider.
- A skip is **not** a failure: it must not set a cooldown, record a usage-limit reset, add a failure-domain exclusion or record affinity for the entry; the entry remains eligible for later, smaller requests within the same chain cycle where routing allows.
- The gate is queue-safe: a context-exceeded skip never enters the contention queue and never triggers remote → local re-routing beyond the ordinary next-provider step.
- Local providers keep the existing `_should_skip_local` behaviour; if `max_context_tokens` is set on a local entry it composes as an **additional hard cap** (effective cap = `min(existing local thresholds, max_context_tokens)`) and never loosens the existing gate.

## Minimal implementation

- `_provider_context_limit(provider_cfg)` reader (mirrors `rate_limit_rpm` parsing in `provider_budget.py`).
- `_should_skip_provider_context(provider_cfg, estimated_tokens)` gate helper.
- Extract the estimate block already inline in `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` into a shared per-request helper (tokenizer + multiplier + `_estimate_effective_prompt_tokens_for_routing`) used by both cycles.
- Enforce the gate for remote entries immediately after `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions`; fold the limit into the local branch's warm-cap computation.
- No `mark_provider_unavailable`, no `_record_sibling_failure`, no affinity, no contention-queue entry for a context-exceeded skip.

## Key Files

- `proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/observability.py`

## Dependencies

- Prerequisite: F1 (context-limit tests).

## Deliverables

Gate code + attempt/log plumbing; F1 tests green; local behaviour unchanged where the field is unset.
data.title: F2: Implement max_context_tokens gate

# Intake Brief: F3 — Ship sourced `max_context_tokens` values

**Headline:** Set documented, sourced `max_context_tokens` limits on the
remote provider entries that have a meaningful ceiling, and leave any
unsourceable entry ungated.

## Goal

Shipped `proxy/config.yaml` expresses real upstream/allowance ceilings so the
free and rate-limited tiers only receive requests they can serve, while the
chain still has a destination for very large prompts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Shipped `proxy/config.yaml` sets a documented, sourced `max_context_tokens` on each remote provider entry whose upstream model or rate allowance has a meaningful ceiling — at minimum `munitoai-free`, `munitoai`, the `opencode-go*` entries and `deepseek-flash` — with the value's source (upstream context window / provider per-minute token allowance) recorded in a config comment.
- No config schema break and no overlay file: `proxy/config.yaml` remains the single authoritative config; an absent field stays a no-op.
- At least one remote tier is left effectively ungated (or capped at the largest upstream context window, e.g. `deepseek-flash`) so an oversized prompt still has a destination and the chain cannot exhaust solely because of caps.
- Config-parsing tests pin the shipped values so drift is caught (extending the pattern in `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`).
- Any limit that cannot be sourced from an upstream context window or a documented provider allowance is left unset, and an OPEN QUESTION is recorded on this item rather than a value being guessed.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `max_context_tokens` to each targeted entry in `proxy/config.yaml` with an adjacent comment naming the source and date.
- Keep the `opencode-go*` (deepseek-v4.1-flash) and `munitoai*` values consistent where the upstream model is identical; document deliberate differences.
- Extend the config pinning test asserted by F1.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`

## Dependencies

- Prerequisite: F2 (reader + gate semantics must exist to pin them).

## Open Question (must resolve during implementation)

- Exact per-entry limit values: each must be sourced (upstream context window
  or the provider's documented per-minute token allowance). If a value cannot
  be sourced, leave the entry ungated and raise it here rather than guessing.
data.title: F3: Ship sourced config limits

# Intake Brief: F4 — Docs and observability for the context gate

**Headline:** Document the `max_context_tokens` field semantics and skip
behaviour across the provider docs, and register the
`provider_context_exceeded` backend-signal counter.

## Goal

An operator adding a provider, or debugging a fall-through, can find the field
in the provider-entry field tables, the skip-behaviour table, and the
observability counters.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the provider-entry field table in `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`, `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/docs/routing.md` (field semantics + skip behaviour table).
- The docs state the field name (`max_context_tokens`), its type, the disabled semantics (absent/`0`/non-positive) and the local-entry composition rule (`min(existing local thresholds, max_context_tokens)`).
- The skip-behaviour table distinguishes a **context-exceeded skip** from a **failure**: no cooldown, no usage-limit quarantine, no failure-domain exclusion, no affinity, no contention-queue entry, and the entry stays eligible for later smaller requests.
- `provider_context_exceeded` is registered in `proxy/observability.py` backend-signal counters (mirroring `context_too_large`) and is surfaced wherever the existing skip reasons are documented.
- Doc examples are copy-pasteable YAML that parse against the shipped schema; no stale reference to a mode overlay is introduced.

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`: add the row/field description alongside `rate_limit_rpm` / `available_times`.
- `proxy/README.md`: mention the gate in the fallback/routing description.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`: semantics paragraph + skip-behaviour table covering `context_too_large`, `large_context_bypass`, `rate_limited` and `provider_context_exceeded`.
- `proxy/observability.py`: add the counter key.

## Key Files

- `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`
- `proxy/README.md`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/observability.py`

## Dependencies

- Prerequisites: F2 (semantics), F3 (shipped values to document).

# Intake Brief: F5 — Full-suite green gate

**Headline:** Verify the change set introduces no regressions: full project
test suite green via the test skill, plus a consistency check across code,
config and docs.

## Goal

The parent item is only releasable when the whole suite passes with the new
gate in place, not just the changed-scope tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (run via the test skill, not an ad-hoc test invocation), with zero new failures attributable to the context-limit gate or the shipped config values.
- Any gate-reported failure is triaged per the test-failure triage policy (critical `test-failure` items via the triage skill) rather than silently ignored.
- Code, `proxy/config.yaml` values and the documentation added by F4 agree on the field name and semantics (no drift between the docs table and the shipped config).
- The audit skill is run against the parent item before advancing it to `in_review`, recording the result.

## Minimal implementation

- Run the suite through `/skill:test`; fix in-scope regressions.
- Cross-check docs vs config vs reader code for naming/semantics drift.
- Run `/skill:audit` on the parent once children are terminal.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/` (whole suite)
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`

## Dependencies

- Prerequisites: F1, F2, F3, F4.
data.title: F5: Full-suite green gate
